## Results of This Work

* Hosted on Zenodo at xxxxx
* Includes:
  * HTML QC/QA reports for every dataset
  * Processed summarized experiments saved as R serialized rds files for every dataset

## Omics Data Repositories

- Journals and funders now require processed data to be deposited in a repository.
- Many support the deposition of raw data in addition to processed data.
- General repositories:
  - Data dryad
  - Zenodo
  - Figshare
- Specific repositories:
  - Gene expression omnibus (GEO): microarrays, gene expression
  - Sequence read archive (SRA): next-gen sequencing
  - Metabolights: metabolomics
  - Metabolomics Workbench: metabolomics

## Metabolomics Workbench

#### Why?

- Because we have a lot of experience downloading, uploading, parsing their files

#### Stats

- Started in XXXX
- Organized by
  - Project: a biological question, contains 1 or more studies
  - Study: further narrowed (maybe), contains 1 or more analyses
  - Analysis: one anlysis method or sample type, NMR, MS + chromatography, +ve / -ve mode, etc
- Currently hosts 4261 studies
- We downloaded **7240 analyses** on 2026-07-21

## Hypothesis

- The majority of data within Metabolomics Workbench (MW) is good.
- Many of the datasets within MW are part of peer-reviewed, published studies.
- Everyone who submits data to MW is trying to do good science.

# Color Grade Evaluation

## Number of Samples in Subject Sample Factors

The number of samples per SSF group indicates if the experimental design is statistically powerful or not.

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

  * all SSF groups have $\le$ 2 samples per group ~ [red]{.my-red};
  * 3 $\le$ all SSF groups $\le$ 4 ~ [yellow]{.my-yellow};
  * all SSF groups $\ge$ 5 samples ~ [green]{.my-green};
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

```{r}
#| label: n-per-group
count_nmostcommon_barplot
```

:::

::::

## Percent Missing and Left-Censorship

High percent missing, especially without the indication of left-censorship indicates the presence of data quality issues.

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

* percent missing $\le$ 2 x SD ~ [green]{.my-green};
* 2 x SD $\lt$ percent missing $\le$ 4 x SD limit ~ [yellow]{.my-yellow};
* percent missing $\gt$ 4 x SD limit ~ [red]{.my-red}
* percent missing $\gt$ 10% & lc test p-value $\le$ 0.05 ~ [green]{.my-green};
* percent missing $\gt$ 10% & lc test p-value $\gt$ 0.05 ~ [yellow]{.my-yellow};

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

```{r}
#| label: percent-missing-plot
data_based_cutoffs_plot$pm
```

:::

::::

## Maximum Observed Median RSD

High maximum observed median RSD indicates high variability in the measurements.

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

* median RSD $\le$ median of medians + 2 x SD ~ [green]{.my-green};
* median of medians + 2 x SD $\lt$ median RSD $\le$ median of medians + 4 x SD ~ [yellow]{.my-yellow};
* median RSD $\gt$ median of medians + 4 x SD ~ [red]{.my-red}
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

```{r}
#| label: max-observed-rsd
data_based_cutoffs_plot$rsd
```

:::

::::

## Median Correlations

Low maximum median ICI-Kt correlation indicates high biological variance between samples.

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column}

* max median ICI-Kt $\ge$ median of max median - 2 SD ~ [green]{.my-green};
* median of max median - 4 SD $\ge$ max median ICI-Kt $\lt$ median of max medians - 2 SD ~ [yellow]{.my-yellow};
* max median ICI-Kt $\lt$ median of max medians - 4 SD ~ [red]{.my-red}

:::

::: {.column}

```{r}
#| label: median-cor-plot
data_based_cutoffs_plot$med_cor
```

:::

::::

## PCA Scores - PC 90

A high PC-90 indicates weak signal variance within the dataset in comparison to other sources of variance present.

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column}

  * PC-90 $\le$ median + 2 SD ~ [green]{.my-green} ; 
  * median + 2 SD $\lt$ PC-90 $\le$ median + 4 SD ~ [yellow]{.my-yellow}; 
  * PC-90 $\gt$ median + 4 SD ~ [red]{.my-red}

::: 

::: {.column}

```{r}
#| label: pc-90-plot
data_based_cutoffs_plot$pc_90
```

:::

::::

## PCA Scores - ANOVA

Lack of separation of SSF groups across meaningful PCs indicates weak signal variance within the dataset.

ANOVA p-adjusted: 

  * p-adjust $\le$ 0.05 & PC-perc $\ge$ 5% & factor is SSF or derived ~ [green]{.my-green}; 
  * p-adjust $\le$ 0.05 & PC-perc $\ge$ 5% & factor is additional sample-data or combination of SSF and additional sample-data ~ [yellow]{.my-yellow};
  * p-adjust $\le$ 0.05 & 1% $\le$ PC-perc $\lt$ 5% ~ [yellow]{.my-yellow};
  * p-adjust $\le$ 0.05 & PC-perc $\lt$ 1% ~ [red]{.my-red};
  * p-adjust $\gt$ 0.05 ~ [red]{.my-red}.

Mean - median ratio (MMR)

## Detection of Log-Transformation


```{r}
#| label: mmr-plot
#| fig-cap: "All plots used datasets with an MMR >= 0.2 and MMR <= 200. **A**: Histogram of Log10(MMR). **B**: Log10(MMR) vs fraction of negative data values, after excluding all datasets with zero negative values. **C**: Histogram of Log10(MMF) for datasets with a maximum observed intensity <= 1000. Vertical lines indicate the MMR cutoffs used of 0.8 (-0.097 on log10 scale) and 1.2 (0.079 on log10 scale) to decide that a dataset should undergo exponentiation."
(mmr_logtransform_plot$mmr_distribution / (mmr_logtransform_plot$mmr_vs_neg | mmr_logtransform_plot$less1000)) + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")
```
